gloss: to drain off moisture; to pat dry

definitions.gloss: to drain off moisture; to pat dry; to wring out water
definitions.explanation: To remove excess water or moisture from food, laundry, or other items. A common cooking and household term.

examples.japanese: {豆腐|とうふ}の{水気|みずけ}を{切|き}る。
examples.english: To drain the moisture from tofu.

examples.japanese: {野菜|やさい}を{洗|あら}ったら、しっかり{水気|みずけ}を{切|き}ってください。
examples.english: After washing the vegetables, please drain them thoroughly.

examples.japanese: {水気|みずけ}を{切|き}らないまま{揚|あ}げると、{油|あぶら}がはねて{危険|きけん}だ。
examples.english: If you fry without draining the moisture, the oil will splatter and it's dangerous.

notes:
USAGE:
Primarily a cooking term. {水気|みずけ} (moisture, water content) + を{切|き}る (to cut/remove). Essential in Japanese cooking where excess moisture affects texture and oil temperature.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水気|みずけ}をよく{切|き}る (to drain well)
- {水気|みずけ}をしっかり{切|き}る (to drain thoroughly)
- キッチンペーパーで{水気|みずけ}を{取|と}る (to remove moisture with a paper towel)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {水|みず}を{切|き}る: to drain water — similar meaning, slightly more general
- {水分|すいぶん}を{飛|と}ばす: to evaporate moisture — using heat rather than draining
